title: Associated primes of a Cohen–Macaulay local ring are minimal primes
statement: Let $(T,\mathfrak n)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (a Noetherian commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$) of Krull dimension $e=\dim T$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] (finite, as $T$ is Noetherian local), and assume that $T$ is Cohen–Macaulay in the sense that $\operatorname{depth}(T)\ge e$ [def-weil-pbc-depth], that is, $\mathfrak n$ contains a $T$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] of length $e$. Let $\mathfrak p\subset T$ be a prime ideal for which there is $z\in T$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_T(z)=\{a\in T: az=0\}=\mathfrak p$ (an associated prime of $T$). Then $\mathfrak p$ is a minimal prime ideal of $T$ (no prime ideal of $T$ is strictly contained in $\mathfrak p$).

proof.text: T is a finite module over itself (Mathlib infers Module.Finite T T). Apply IsLocalRing.depth_le_ringKrullDim_quotient_of_mem_associatedPrimes to p and hp, then compose with the hypothesis e <= depth(T), using the order-preserving coercion from ENat to WithBot ENat. This gives e <= dim(T/p).

proof.text: Use Mathlib minimalPrimes_eq_minimals: p is prime because it is associated, so it remains to show p <= q for every prime q <= p. Suppose p is not contained in q, and choose x in p but outside q. The quotient T/q is a domain, so the nonzero image of x is a nonzerodivisor. The surjective quotient factor map T/q -> T/p kills that image. Mathlib ringKrullDim_succ_le_of_surjective (Mathlib.RingTheory.KrullDimension.NonZeroDivisors) therefore gives dim(T/p)+1 <= dim(T/q). Mathlib ringKrullDim_quotient_le gives dim(T/q) <= dim(T)=e. Combined with the first step this gives e+1 <= e in WithBot ENat. Cast this finite inequality back to Nat and contradict Nat.not_succ_le_self. Thus p is minimal. This is the dimension-strictness argument of Stacks 0BUS, using Mathlib's packaged chain inequality instead of constructing a chain explicitly.
